message.content:
`docker start` is used to start **containers**, not the Docker engine itself.  
To bring the Docker service up on Windows you have a couple of options:

| Method | What it does | How to run it |
|--------|--------------|---------------|
| **Docker Desktop** | Launches the Docker Desktop GUI, which automatically starts the Docker Engine. | Double‑click the Docker Desktop icon on your desktop or start menu. |
| **PowerShell** | Starts the Windows Service that runs the Docker Engine. | ```powershell\nStart-Service Docker\n``` |
| **Command Prompt** | Same as PowerShell but using `net start`. | ```cmd\nnet start com.docker.service\n``` |

If you’re using Docker Toolbox (the legacy “docker-machine” setup), you would instead run:

```powershell
docker-machine start default
```

Once the Docker service is running, you can verify it with:

```powershell
docker info
```

That will show you the Docker Engine version and other details, confirming that Docker is up and ready.
